stops.title: Houghton in Domesday Book
stops.text: Domesday Book lists Houghton in the hundred of Redbornestoke. Adeliza de Grandmesnil held it from the king, and a man called Arnold held the land from her.

stops.title: The village shop
stops.text: A house is built in the village partly from an old manor house, most likely Conquestbury. Today it is the village shop and post office.

stops.title: The east window
stops.text: John William Burgon, Dean of Chichester, gives All Saints its stained-glass east window, in memory of three benefactors.

stops.title: The Church of All Saints
stops.text: The parish church is built in the 14th century, with a nave, aisles, a chancel and a battlemented tower with six bells. Over the north door a large St Christopher is painted in the 15th century; traces of other wall paintings can still be seen.

stops.title: The Conquest family
stops.text: From the 13th to the 18th century the Conquest family held a manor here, and the village took their name: Houghton Conquest. Their house, Conquestbury, stood where Bury Farm is now, beside London Lane. When the family left, it was let fall into ruin.

stops.title: Houghton House
stops.text: Mary Sidney, Countess of Pembroke, poet and patron, starts a great house on the ridge, possibly with Inigo Jones. James I visits in 1621, soon after it is finished; the Countess dies of smallpox that September.

stops.title: House Beautiful
stops.text: John Bunyan publishes The Pilgrim's Progress. Houghton House, on the ridge south of the village, is said to be his House Beautiful, where Christian is welcomed on his way.

stops.title: The roof comes off
stops.text: The 5th Duke of Bedford has Houghton House stripped: the furnishings go and the roof is sold off as building material. The staircase ended up in the Swan Hotel in Bedford. The walls still stand.

stops.title: King's Wood and Glebe Meadows
stops.text: The ash and maple wood and the old meadows south of the village become a Site of Special Scientific Interest. Their rare plants had been found by a local teenager, Peter Sollars.
